headline: Orissa HC sets aside Sales Tax Commissioner's order passed ignoring adjournment plea
reference: M/s. SMV Beverages Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Odisha, Orissa High Court, W.P.(C) Nos. 16677, 16800 & 17164 of 2026, order dated 18.11.2026
summary_points: Issue: Whether the Commissioner of Sales Tax (Odisha) could decide OST Act appeals without considering an adjournment plea filed on the hearing date.
Held: The CA entrusted with the case had undergone surgery; the plea was not considered, violating natural justice. The order dated 07.01.2026 was set aside.
Court noted that each adjournment plea must be judged on its own reason, not on the number of earlier adjournments (relying on Chandra Govindji, (2000) 8 SCC 532).
Appeals under Section 23(4)(c) of the Odisha Sales Tax Act, 1947 are restored; the Commissioner must rehear them and give reasonable opportunity.
The merits (revision of IPR 1996 exemptions for AY 1996-97 to 1998-99) were not decided; only the procedural lapse was addressed.
who_is_affected: Dealers and taxpayers with appeals pending before tax appellate authorities, and the Odisha CT & GST organisation.
action_required: Appellate authorities should record and decide adjournment requests with reasons, and taxpayers should file documented requests on time and follow up on their outcome.

Orissa High Court: an appeal order passed without considering an adjournment plea violates natural justice.

In M/s. SMV Beverages Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Odisha (W.P.(C) Nos. 16677, 16800 and 17164 of 2026, order dated 18.11.2026), the Commissioner of Sales Tax decided appeals under Section 23(4)(c) of the Odisha Sales Tax Act, 1947 on 07.01.2026. The hearing had been fixed for 20.12.2025, and the petitioner's adjournment plea was filed on 19 and 20 December because its Chartered Accountant had undergone major surgery. The plea was not considered.

The Court held:
- Each adjournment request must be examined independently, regardless of earlier adjournments.
- What matters is the reasonableness of time granted, not the number of adjournments.
- The petitioner was denied a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

The order was set aside and the appeals were restored for fresh hearing. The merits of the exemption dispute for AY 1996-97 to 1998-99 were not decided.

Practical takeaway: file adjournment requests in writing with supporting documents, and confirm the outcome before the hearing date.
